title: Which division gives the largest answer?
description: Three divisions of nine are ranked by looking only at the divisors, and then checked by working them out. The smaller the divisor, the greater the quotient. Keeko raises the doubt that the biggest divisor gives the largest answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: the smaller the divisor, the greater the quotient. Watch for students who think the biggest divisor gives the biggest quotient.

source: Without finding the quotients, say which of 9 ÷ (3/2), 9 ÷ (
video_script.why: A learner ranks quotients by thinking about the divisors first, and then checks the ranking by working the quotients out.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own talk question, nine, three halves, two thirds and one
video_script.anchor: the three divisions of nine, with the divisors placed on a number line against one
video_script.wrong_answer: three halves gives the largest answer
video_script.wrong_move: thinks the biggest divisor gives the largest quotient
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty seven halves is the largest, and six is the smallest

final_answer.value: 27/2 is the largest, and 6 is the smallest
final_answer.spoken: twenty seven halves is the largest, and six is the smallest

video_script.fraction_reading: three halves, two thirds, twenty seven halves
maths_rules: 3/2 is above 1, 2/3 is between 0 and 1, and 1 is 1
6 < 9 < 27/2, so 9 ÷ 3/2 is the smallest and 9 ÷ 2/3 is the largest
video_script.design: A number line with the three quotients placed in order, smallest to largest, and the divisors shown against one.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the divisions 9 ÷ 3/2, 9 ÷ 2/3 and 9 ÷ 1 in a row

marks.pose: the three divisions arrive in a row
marks.ask: a question mark glows above the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about comparing quotients.
<bookmark mark='pose'/>Nine divided by three halves, nine divided by two thirds, and nine divided by one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Without working them out, which is largest and which is smallest?

beats.on_screen: the three divisions stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number line with 1 marked in the accent colour; 9 ÷ 1 = 9 written beside it

marks.ask: the number line arrives with one marked
marks.ref: nine divided by one is written beside the line

narration: <bookmark mark='ask'/>Dividing nine by a number asks how many of that number fit in nine.
<bookmark mark='ref'/>Nine divided by one leaves nine, so it is our reference.

marks.given: the dividend and the three divisors are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the dividend is nine, and the divisors are three halves, two thirds and one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the largest and the smallest of the three quotients

marks.find: the words To find and the three divisions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to rank the three quotients from smallest to largest.

beats.on_screen: 3/2 is above 1; 2/3 is between 0 and 1; the third divisor is 1

marks.cmp: each divisor is placed against the mark for one
marks.first: three halves lands beyond one, and two thirds lands before one

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step one, compare each divisor with one.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Three halves is above one, and two thirds is between zero and one.

beats.on_screen: 9 ÷ 3/2 < 9 ÷ 1 < 9 ÷ 2/3: the smaller the divisor, the greater the quotient

marks.less: a divisor above one puts the quotient before nine
marks.more: a divisor between zero and one puts the quotient beyond nine
marks.order: the three divisions are lined up in order

narration: <bookmark mark='less'/>Step two, a divisor above one gives a quotient less than nine.
<bookmark mark='more'/>A divisor between zero and one gives a quotient greater than nine.
<bookmark mark='order'/>Nine divided by one is nine itself, so the smallest divisor gives the largest quotient.

marks.small: nine times two thirds is written under the first division
marks.mid: nine divided by one is written under the third division

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step three, check the smallest. Nine divided by three halves is nine times two thirds, which is six.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Nine divided by one is nine.

marks.big: nine times three halves is written under the second division
marks.mult: the tops are multiplied over the bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Step four, check the largest. Nine divided by two thirds is nine times three halves.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>That is nine times three on top, over two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 9 ÷ 2/3 = 27/2 is the largest; 9 ÷ 3/2 = 6 is the smallest
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Nine divided by two thirds is twenty seven halves, and nine divided by three halves is six.
Twenty seven halves is the largest, and six is the smallest.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the biggest divisor gives the biggest quotient; the number line shows 6 before 9 and 27/2 beyond 9

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble ranks the quotients by the size of the divisor
marks.slip: the number line shows six before nine
marks.fix: the order of the quotients is reversed

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three halves gives the largest answer, because it is the biggest divisor.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But a bigger divisor fits into nine fewer times, so the answer is smaller.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The smaller the divisor, the greater the quotient.
